title: URL Versioning
description: Implement API versioning using URL paths, including route structure, documentation, migration, and deprecation timelines.

data.text: URL versioning embeds the API version directly in the path: /v1/users, /v2/users. It is the most visible and widely adopted versioning strategy. Clients can see the version at a glance, and deprecation is as simple as returning 404 on an old path.
Place the version as the first path segment. This makes routing simple and documentation clear. Every versioned endpoint follows the same path pattern.

data.title: URL versioning with route constraints in C#
data.content: Use API versioning attributes to keep controllers organized by version while sharing business logic.

data.text: When retiring a version, return 410 Gone for old paths after the sunset date. Include a Deprecation header and a Link to the migration guide.

data.title: Deprecated v1 response
data.content: After the sunset date, v1 endpoints return 410 Gone with helpful headers.

data.title: Keep v1 running during migration
data.text: Publish a 12-month deprecation timeline. Monitor v1 traffic weekly. When active v1 clients drop below 5%, accelerate the sunset date. When they drop below 1%, return 410 Gone immediately.

items.question: Does URL versioning cause code duplication?
items.answer: Share business logic through internal services. Controllers should only translate between external contracts and internal models. If you find yourself copying controllers, extract a shared adapter layer.

items.question: What versioning scheme should I use?
items.answer: Use simple integer versions (v1, v2) or date-based versions (v2026-10). Integer versions are easier for humans; date versions are better for continuous deployment.

items.question: Should I version every endpoint?
items.answer: Only version endpoints that change. If v2 only adds a field to GET /users, you can return the new field in v1 as an additive, non-breaking change and skip v2 entirely.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: URL versioning is the most explicit and debuggable strategy.
Share logic through services, not through duplicated controllers.
410 Gone with migration links is the professional way to sunset a version.
Monitor version traffic to accelerate or extend deprecation timelines.
data.takeaway: URL versioning makes the API contract visible in every request. That visibility is a feature, not a burden.
